notes: This focal postflight closes the PROF-PRIVATE-CHAT remote-open failure and same-action retry boundary on Web/Wasm, Android and iOS. An authenticated actor opens the peer public profile from Chat, receives a bounded forced transport error, retries through the same Chat action and reaches the existing private conversation; the coordinator verifies exactly one matching private thread through authenticated RPC.

The evidence-only one-shot hooks bypass a warm private-thread cache, raise the forced failure at the remote-open boundary immediately before the authenticated transport call and keep bypassing the cache until the retry completes that real call. Android is debug-only, Web is localhost-only and iOS receives the hook only through the XCTest launch environment. Production cache, authentication and conversation semantics remain unchanged.

Android and Web passed while the working tree was based on c3ac1e82 with the reviewed transport-forcing diff present. That exact diff was committed as 47cf28c9 and rebased byte-equivalently as c8eae71b. The later 99617533 commit, rebased as ab6af826, changes only the focal iOS XCTest startup precondition from Feed to any authenticated surface. The inherited 87d8b20d tree was byte-identical to main at cd1ea064; reconciliation changed no product bytes, so the Android and Web focal matrices were not repeated solely for new commit identifiers.

The first Android attempt on API 37 stopped before product interaction because its Espresso runtime could not resolve InputManager; the accepted run used the supported API 35 image. Web exposed and corrected the warm-cache bypass and a recomposition that temporarily dropped the test-tag aria while leaving the same visible Chat control. The first iOS build exhausted VM disk space; after deleting only generated outputs, the next XCTest completed the target flow but retained a failure from an unrelated Feed-only startup assertion. The accepted clean-SHA rerun uses the authenticated-surface preflight already used by neighboring focal tests.

All accepted runners verified actor binding, the same peer, visible failure, retry through the same UI action, exact private-conversation navigation, uniqueness of the backend private thread and zero physical residue for the owned temporary fixture.

The committed reports are sanitized projections. Raw reports, screenshots, UI logs, the iOS result bundle and the failed-attempt history are kept in private host custody recorded outside the repository. Credentials, raw identifiers and local diagnostic paths are omitted from the repository.
This reduction does not certify concurrent repeated taps or races between different profile actions; that boundary remains separate.
